headline: A Japanese factory that once made iPhone screens is to be turned into a plant for the base boards that hold AI chips, Nikkei Asia reports.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: the article itself could not be read, so the investment, start date and output are unknown.
importance_line: A new Japanese source of package substrates, the base boards that carry a chip, would add capacity for AI chip makers, but the investment size, start date and output are not known.
summary: Nikkei Asia reports that the Mobara factory of Japan Display (JDI), which once made LCD screens for iPhones, will now make package substrates, the base boards on which chips are mounted, for Shinko Electric Industries, its fifth owner, and Digitimes carries the same account.
notes: Nikkei Asia is subscription-only; summary rests on its headline, standfirst and opening paragraph, with Digitimes' preview as a second outlet. Summary kept to one cautious sentence.
